A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TruthRL. All 18 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison. Earlier analyses can be matched despite substantial relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and evaluation results across four knowledge-intensive benchmarks, alongside reward ablations, model-scaling experiments and behavioral analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, reward-sensitivity experiments, GSM8K evaluation and a 70B-model comparison.

M1.justification: The proposed GRPO procedure and default rewards remain +1 for correct answers, 0 for abstention and -1 for hallucination. Knowledge-enhanced and reasoning-enhanced variants are retained. New reward-value experiments are ablations, rather than changes to the proposed default method.

E1.justification: v2 adds GSM8K mathematical reasoning evaluation in Table 7, extending testing beyond knowledge-intensive QA into a distinct task domain. CRAG training and evaluation on CRAG, NQ, HotpotQA and MuSiQue remain, including retrieval and non-retrieval coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated RLHF and RLKF baselines across both backbones and retrieval settings. Appendix A, Table 12 adds GPT-5 and OpenAI o3 comparisons against prompting and TruthRL with Llama3.3-70B-Instruct. RLCR, SaySelf and RewardingDoubt appear only in a conceptual comparison, not as experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds bounded experimental settings: training abstention rewards of -0.5, 0 and 0.5, evaluation abstention weights at those values, and a 70B backbone. Hallucination becomes an auxiliary rather than co-primary metric. Previously reported default training and inference settings remain unchanged; these additions do not establish reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: New analyses examine group-dependent abstention dynamics in Figure 3, neutral reward selection in Table 5, metric-weight sensitivity in Table 6 and transfer to mathematical reasoning in Table 7. Appendix E adds a judge-output case study. Earlier verifier, scaling, DPO and reasoning-reward analyses are retained, largely in Appendix A.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-run variability, statistical confidence intervals, significance tests or statistical error bars. The retained confidence-bin analysis concerns model-output confidence, not uncertainty in experimental estimates.

E6.justification: All 24 retained Table 1 rows and the matched earlier analysis tables preserve their numerical results. Substantial new results cover added baselines, sensitivity tests, GSM8K and 70B comparisons. GSM8K reports TruthRL truthfulness 71.9, hallucination 12.7 and accuracy 84.6. Table 12 reports average truthfulness/hallucination of 29.9/21.0 for 70B TruthRL versus 36.8/28.3 for GPT-5. These are additional findings, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 changes the truthfulness definition's admissible weights: v1 requires all three weights to be nonnegative, whereas v2 allows the abstention weight to depend on deployment needs, including negative values. GRPO, advantage and DPO equations remain equivalent; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central ternary-reward and knowledge-boundary claims persist, but headline comparisons change. v1 emphasizes average gains over vanilla RL of 21.1 points in truthfulness and 28.9 points in hallucination reduction. v2's abstract instead uses the retained CRAG prompting comparison, while its conclusion's 43.4/40.1 figures match the SFT comparison in the retained Llama retrieval block. These reframe the claimed advantage without changing those results.

C2.justification: v2 adds group-dependent credit explanations, attributes knowledge-enhancement limitations to static probing, and interprets new experiments as supporting neutral rewards, domain transfer and competitiveness with production models. Section 4.3 also strengthens abstaining 'mostly' when knowledge is lacking to 'only' when it is lacking, although the corresponding difficult-question results are unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a TruthRL code-access link and specifies temperature 0.6 and top-p 0.9 for the existing 256-response knowledge-probing procedure. This is additional disclosure, not evidence that probing changed. Most hardware, retrieval, training and inference details are retained in Appendix C; prompt templates gain explicit section delimiters.

R1.justification: The earlier related-work discussion is retained and substantially expanded in Appendix B. A new confidence-calibration-versus-abstention subsection and Table 13 position TruthRL relative to RLCR, SaySelf and RewardingDoubt. Numerous additional factuality, uncertainty and abstention references broaden the research positioning beyond a simple relocation.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: the abstract is shortened, method explanations expand, several experimental discussions move into Additional Analysis, and detailed related work moves behind a condensed main-text section. Appendices expand from implementation details and prompts to five sections. Impact and acknowledgement sections are added.

P2.justification: The main text and bibliography change from a single-column report to a two-column conference layout. v2 adds an abstention-dynamics figure and six tables, expands Table 1 with baseline rows, changes highlighting conventions and relocates several existing displays. The earlier figures and tables remain identifiable.

improvement.justification: The added RL baselines and direct tests of reward and metric choices strengthen support for the central design; GSM8K adds useful transfer evidence, and expanded related work clarifies positioning. However, settings for new comparisons remain sparsely documented, and the strengthened claim that abstention occurs 'only' outside the model's knowledge exceeds what the retained analysis establishes. These tradeoffs support a limited net improvement.
